title: Induced metric and the Nambu area
notes: For a map \(x:\mathcal E\to\mathbb R^d\), the notes put \(g_{ij}=(\partial_i x,\partial_j x)\), call this a Riemannian metric, and define \(\mathcal L(x)=\int_{\mathcal E}\sqrt{\det g}\,d\xi_1d\xi_2\). Both Euclidean and Minkowski target metrics are mentioned.
statement: Let \(x:\Sigma\to\mathbb R^d\) be a smooth immersion of an oriented surface, with compact domain or convergent area integral. In a Euclidean target its pullback metric \(h=x^*\langle\ ,\ \rangle\) is positive definite and \(A(x)=\int_\Sigma d\operatorname{vol}_h\) is coordinate independent. In a Lorentzian target this same formula applies to a spacelike immersion. For a timelike world sheet the real area density instead uses \(\sqrt{|\det h|}\).
reconstruction: Immersion, the signature of the induced metric, and integrability are supplied hypotheses. An arbitrary map may have a degenerate pullback, and one negative target direction does not imply a Riemannian world sheet.
fate: This is the classical geometric starting point of \citet[eq.~(3)]{polyakov1981quantum}, published 23 July 1981.
present_status: As of November 2026: An established definition with essential signature and nondegeneracy qualifications; no new problem is posed.

title: A symbolic sum over surfaces with marked target points
notes: The functional integral \(\int\exp(i\mathcal L/\hbar)\mathcal D x\) is taken over surfaces passing through prescribed points. Reparametrization invariance is stated.
statement: For a specified surface \(\Sigma\), marked points \(p_a\), and target values \(y_a\), the constraint \(x(p_a)=y_a\) defines a space of parametrized maps. Area is invariant under diffeomorphisms preserving the marked data. The displayed oscillatory integral is a formal expression until a regularization, quotient, measure, and limiting prescription have been supplied.
reconstruction: The distinction between fixed marked domain points and an unparametrized image merely containing the target points is not resolved in the notebook. Neither is the choice between fixed topology and a sum over topologies.
fate: The formal surface-sum program is already explicit in \citet[eqs.~(1)--(3)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Identifiable exposition, not a defined probability or oscillatory measure theorem. Its missing choices preclude a single problem-index entry.

title: First variation of area and the minimal-surface equation
notes: The first variation is written \(\delta\mathcal L=-\int(\delta x,\Delta x)\), and \(\Delta x=0\) is called the minimal-surface equation.
statement: For a smooth immersed surface in Euclidean space, use its induced metric \(h\) and the nonpositive Laplacian \(\Delta_h=\operatorname{div}_h\nabla_h\). If the variation field \(V\) is compactly supported away from the boundary, then \(\delta A(V)=-\int_\Sigma\langle V,\Delta_hx\rangle\,d\operatorname{vol}_h\). Thus stationarity for all such \(V\) is equivalent to vanishing mean-curvature vector, with \(\Delta_hx\) equal to its trace convention. A closed connected surface has no nonconstant Euclidean harmonic coordinate map.
reconstruction: The measure, boundary condition, induced-metric dependence, and mean-curvature normalization are made explicit. This is not the linear harmonic-map equation for an independently fixed metric.
fate: The same classical equation occurs in \citet[eq.~(5)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: The geometric first-variation statement is correct with these hypotheses; the closed Euclidean case also explains why nontrivial saddles need additional data.

title: Gelfand on harmonic maps and the construction of minimal surfaces
notes: Gelfand refers to Eells and to a group recorded as \ru{Лашоф}, in connection with constructing minimal surfaces.
statement: A conformal harmonic immersion of a Riemann surface into Euclidean space has minimal image. The note does not specify a theorem, ambient manifold, topology, or construction attached to either name.
reconstruction: Only the general harmonic/conformal implication can be formulated. The manuscript spelling is retained: replacing it by Lawson, Lashof, or a particular joint paper would be conjectural identification.
fate: The named publication has not been identified. The nearby classical statement is documented in \citet[eqs.~(5)--(7)]{polyakov1981quantum}; that is not evidence for the personal attribution.
present_status: As of November 2026: Historical attribution unresolved; no orphan research question can be extracted from this sentence.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The proposed second variation of area
notes: At a critical surface the notes assert \(\delta^2\mathcal L=-\int(\Delta\delta x,\delta x)\), followed by a quadratic Taylor expansion.
statement: For a Euclidean minimal immersion and a compactly supported normal variation \(V\), the area Hessian is \(\int_\Sigma(|\nabla^\perp V|^2-\sum_{a,b}\langle A_{ab},V\rangle^2)\,d\operatorname{vol}_h\), where \(A\) is the second fundamental form and the tangent frame is orthonormal. For a fixed metric \(g\), the Hessian of \(\frac12\int|dx|_g^2\) is instead \(-\int\langle V,\Delta_gV\rangle\,d\operatorname{vol}_g\). A Taylor expansion uses one half of the Hessian and a remainder of order smaller than the quadratic term.
reconstruction: The notebook conflates two functionals. An elementary check already disproves its unrestricted claim: on a planar disk, take a nonzero smooth tangential field vanishing near the boundary and a sufficiently small reparametrization \(x_t(u,v)=(u+t f(u,v),v)\). Its image and area are fixed, whereas the displayed Dirichlet quadratic form is \(\int|\nabla f|^2>0\). This is an editorial countercheck, not a new result attributed to Feigin. Editorial area-versus-energy countercheck \ours.
fate: The distinction between varying the induced metric and an independent metric is explicit in \citet[eqs.~(3),(6)--(7)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: False literally. The classical Jacobi formula and the fixed-metric energy formula are established; no C/D problem survives the correction.

title: Dirichlet energy and independent variation of the metric
notes: The area expression is replaced by \(\mathcal L'(x,g)=\int g^{ij}(\partial_i x,\partial_jx)\sqrt g\,d^2\xi\), and on the next page \(x\) and \(g\) are declared independent variables.
statement: On a smooth compact surface, with fixed boundary values if there is boundary, set \(E_g(x)=\frac12\int g^{ij}\partial_i x\cdot\partial_jx\,d\operatorname{vol}_g\). Map variation gives \(\Delta_gx=0\). Metric variation gives \(T_{ij}=\partial_i x\cdot\partial_jx-\frac12g_{ij}|dx|_g^2=0\). For an immersion into a Euclidean target, \(T=0\) means \(x^*\langle\ ,\ \rangle=\lambda g\), \(\lambda>0\). On such pairs \(E_g=A(x)\); the notebook's normalization without \(1/2\) gives \(2A(x)\).
reconstruction: The stress-tensor equation and the factor of two repair the omitted logical step. Weyl invariance in two dimensions leaves the scalar \(\lambda\) undetermined.
fate: This is Polyakov's already published independent-metric reformulation \citep[eqs.~(6)--(7)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: The classical equivalence is established for nondegenerate critical maps, with the stated boundary conditions and normalization.

title: Harmonicity does not force conformality
notes: The text says that at an extremum of the fixed-metric functional the induced metric is conformal to the chosen metric.
statement: Harmonicity \(\Delta_gx=0\) by itself does not imply conformality. On a planar domain with \(g=du^2+dv^2\), \(x(u,v)=(2u,v)\) is a harmonic immersion, but \(x^*g_{\mathbb R^2}=4du^2+dv^2\) is not conformal to \(g\). Conformality follows after also imposing the metric Euler--Lagrange equation \(T=0\).
reconstruction: This counterexample fixes the boundary values to those of \(x\), so it is an actual critical point of the Dirichlet problem. It checks both the hypothesis and the failed conclusion, independently of the area-Hessian countercheck. Editorial harmonic nonconformal counterexample \ours.
fate: The missing second variational equation is present in \citet[eq.~(7)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: The literal implication is false; its corrected version is classical. No open problem is created by the omission.

title: The weak L2 metric on the space of metrics
notes: The notebook defines \(\|\theta\|_g^2=\int\theta_{ij}\theta_{k\ell}g^{ik}g^{j\ell}\sqrt g\,d\xi_1d\xi_k\) and calls \(\mathcal Dg\) its formal volume form.
statement: For a closed smooth surface \(\Sigma\), the space of positive smooth symmetric 2-tensors has tangent space \(\Gamma(S^2T^*\Sigma)\). Its positive weak Riemannian pairing is \(G_g(\theta,\psi)=\int_\Sigma\operatorname{tr}(g^{-1}\theta g^{-1}\psi)\,d\operatorname{vol}_g\). The coordinate measure is \(d\xi_1d\xi_2\). This infinite-dimensional pairing does not, by itself, define a locally finite Lebesgue-type volume measure.
reconstruction: The last differential is an index error in the notebook. The distinction between a weak metric and an actual measure is essential, not an extra choice of normalization.
fate: The metric-measure heuristic belongs to the earlier gauge-fixed path integral \citep[eqs.~(14),(17)--(20)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: The weak metric is well defined; its formal volume notation remains formal.

title: Diffeomorphism redundancy and Faddeev--Popov gauge fixing
notes: The integrand is constant on diffeomorphism orbits, the integral is said to be undefined, and the \ru{трюк Фаддеева--Попова} is proposed.
statement: The action on pairs \((x,g)\) is invariant under \((x,g)\mapsto(x\circ f,f^*g)\). Locally, gauge fixing replaces orbit directions by a Jacobian built from the infinitesimal action, together with residual automorphism and moduli factors. This is a prescription for a regularized functional integral; it is not justified by literally dividing two infinite volumes.
reconstruction: A slice, treatment of stabilizers, and determinant regularization are additions needed to formulate the method. The notebook does not prove existence of a quotient measure.
fate: The concrete string application is in \citet[eqs.~(17)--(23)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established formal gauge-fixing machinery, with rigorous finite-dimensional and elliptic ingredients distinguished from the full path integral.

title: Dolbeault Laplacians and primed zeta determinants
notes: For a complex curve with a compatible metric, \(T\) is its holomorphic tangent bundle, \(T^j\) its tensor power, and \(\Delta_j=\bar\partial^*\bar\partial\). The notes write \(\zeta(s)=\sum\lambda_i^{-s}\) and \(\log\operatorname{Det}\Delta=-\zeta'(0)\).
statement: Let \(\Sigma\) be a closed Riemann surface with a smooth positive metric, let \(j\in\mathbb Z\), and use the induced Hermitian metric on \(T^j\). The positive elliptic operator \(\Delta_j\) has discrete spectrum. Set \(\zeta_j(s)=\sum_{\lambda>0}\lambda^{-s}\), initially for \(\Re s>1\), and \(\det'\Delta_j=\exp[-\zeta'_j(0)]\) by its meromorphic continuation, regular at zero. The prime excludes \(H^0(T^j)\).
reconstruction: Compactness, integer tensor powers, the Hilbert-space realization, and exclusion of zero eigenvalues are implicit in the notes. Without the prime, zero modes make the displayed definition meaningless.
fate: The definition and its use for Cauchy--Riemann operators are in \citet[\S3]{quillen1985determinants}, received June 1984 and published in the first 1985 issue.
present_status: As of November 2026: A standard spectral determinant, distinct from an ordinary infinite product.

title: The formal logarithmic derivative needs regularization
notes: The notebook factors \(\operatorname{Det}(\Delta+\varepsilon\delta\Delta)\) and obtains \(\delta\log\operatorname{Det}\Delta=\operatorname{Tr}(\delta\Delta\,\Delta^{-1})\).
statement: For a smooth family of positive invertible elliptic operators \(A_t\) of fixed order on a closed manifold, the meaningful variation is \(\frac d{dt}\log\det_\zeta A_t=\operatorname{FP}_{s=0}\operatorname{Tr}(\dot A_tA_t^{-s-1})\), where \(\operatorname{FP}\) denotes the constant Laurent coefficient. With constant-dimensional kernels one works on their complements and includes the changing zero-mode metrics when forming a determinant line. In finite dimension this reduces to the ordinary trace formula.
reconstruction: The formal quotient of differential operators is not generally trace class. Zeta determinants are not universally multiplicative, so the factorization is not an independent proof of the variation formula. The finite-part formula follows by differentiating the zeta function where the trace converges and continuing meromorphically. Editorial differentiation of the zeta function \ours; the determinant framework and nonmultiplicativity reference are prior literature.
fate: The zeta-function and determinant-line framework predates the talk \citep[\S3]{quillen1985determinants}. The failure of general multiplicativity is explicitly analyzed in \citet[\S1, especially \S1.1]{kontsevichvishik1994geometry}, circulated in April/June 1994. This later reference verifies the limitation; it does not turn the notebook's formal derivative into a new 1985 discovery.
present_status: As of November 2026: The regularized derivative is established; the notebook's unqualified determinant multiplication is false as a general rule.

title: Conformal change of the Dolbeault adjoint
notes: For \(g\mapsto(1+\varepsilon\rho)g\), the page gives \(\Delta+\varepsilon\delta\Delta=(1+\varepsilon\rho)^j\bar\partial^*(1+\varepsilon\rho)^{-j-1}\bar\partial\).
statement: Write \(g'=e^\varphi g\). For sections of the tangent power \(T^j\), the \(L^2\) inner products in Dolbeault degrees zero and one scale by \(e^{(j+1)\varphi}\) and \(e^{j\varphi}\). Therefore \(\bar\partial^*_{g'}=e^{-(j+1)\varphi}\bar\partial^*_g e^{j\varphi}\), and \(\Delta_{j,g'}=e^{-(j+1)\varphi}\bar\partial^*_g e^{j\varphi}\bar\partial\). The displayed notebook formula is instead this expression with \(j\) replaced by \(-j-1\).
reconstruction: This is a direct adjoint calculation using the explicitly declared tangent-bundle convention. The printed expression is the formula for the Serre-dual bundle \(T^{-j-1}\), whose nonzero spectrum is related to that of \(T^j\). Such duality does not make the two differential operators literally equal. Editorial conformal-adjoint computation \oursComputed.
fate: The elliptic-complex metric convention is fixed in \citet[\S3]{quillen1985determinants}; the distinction is checked here directly.
present_status: As of November 2026: The operator formula requires the dual-bundle correction or a declared change of convention. Its symmetric determinant anomaly can nevertheless agree.

title: Heat finite parts and the one-dimensional regularization ambiguity
notes: The trace of multiplication by \(\rho\) is regulated by \(\operatorname{Tr}(\rho e^{-t\Delta})=a_{-1}(\rho)t^{-1}+a_0(\rho)+\cdots\). On the codimension-one kernel of \(a_{-1}\) it has a finite limit; extension is written \(\kappa a_{-1}+a_0\).
statement: For a Laplace-type operator on a smooth closed surface and smooth \(\rho\), the heat trace has this expansion. Its finite part is \(a_0(\rho)\). If a linear regularization functional agrees with \(a_0\) on \(\ker a_{-1}\), and \(a_{-1}\ne0\), then elementary linear algebra forces it to equal \(a_0+\kappa a_{-1}\) for a scalar \(\kappa\).
reconstruction: The uniqueness claim concerns a functional at a fixed metric with this agreement condition. It does not classify all metric-dependent, nonlocal, or nonlinear renormalization schemes. Zero modes change the finite part if one replaces the full heat trace by a primed trace. Editorial linear-algebra deduction of the one-dimensional extension ambiguity \ours; the heat expansion itself is classical.
fate: The heat expansion is classical \citep[opening heat-kernel formulas]{mckeansinger1967curvature}; the extension assertion is the linear-algebra argument just stated.
present_status: As of November 2026: A valid finite-part prescription with an explicitly limited ambiguity, not an unresolved renormalization theorem.

title: The scalar heat coefficient and curvature convention
notes: The expansion is \((4\pi t)^{-1}[\int\rho+(t/3)\int\rho K+\cdots]\), but \(K\) is called scalar curvature. The subsequent finite-trace line drops \(1/(4\pi)\).
statement: For the nonnegative scalar Laplace--Beltrami operator on a closed Riemannian surface, \(\operatorname{Tr}(\rho e^{-t\Delta})=(4\pi t)^{-1}\int\rho\,dA+(24\pi)^{-1}\int\rho R\,dA+O(t)\), with scalar curvature \(R=2K_G\). Thus the bracket coefficient is \(R/6=K_G/3\).
reconstruction: The displayed coefficient is consistent with Gaussian curvature, not with the accompanying scalar-curvature label. A Dolbeault Laplacian differing by a fixed factor changes the time normalization but not this finite coefficient. A realified complex line doubles both trace coefficients.
fate: The source named in the notes is correctly identifiable as \citet{mckeansinger1967curvature}; the original appeared in 1967, its Russian translation in 1969.
present_status: As of November 2026: A normalization error in an old heat-kernel formula. The manuscript, rather than the transcription, contains the conflicting label.

title: Tensor-spin heat coefficients and Serre symmetry
notes: For \(T^j\) the page writes a leading coefficient twice the scalar one and a curvature coefficient \(j+2/3\). It then pairs \(j\) with \(-j-1\).
statement: Serre duality on a closed Riemann surface pairs \(H^1(T^j)\) with \(H^0(K\otimes(T^j)^{-1})=H^0(T^{-j-1})\). With compatible metrics, the nonzero singular values of the Dolbeault complex give the corresponding dual spectral pairing. A complex trace, its underlying real trace, and the normalizations of \(\bar\partial^*\bar\partial\) and the scalar Laplacian must be fixed before numerical heat coefficients can be compared.
reconstruction: The dual exponent is unambiguous. The isolated coefficient \(j+2/3\) is not certified as an exact invariant formula because the notebook changes real/complex and operator conventions; the anomaly polynomial is treated separately.
fate: The cohomological interpretation is already part of the determinant-line construction \citep[\S\S1--3]{quillen1985determinants}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Duality is established; the shorthand coefficient remains normalization-dependent and cannot be used unqualified.

title: The quadratic anomaly coefficient
notes: The conformal variation contains a curvature term proportional to \(6j^2+6j+1\), and an area term involving a regularization constant.
statement: For the Dolbeault determinant line of \(T^j=K^{-j}\) on a closed curve, with its induced Hodge and zeta-corrected metric, the local gravitational anomaly relative to that of \(\mathcal O\) has coefficient \(a_j=6j^2+6j+1\). It satisfies \(a_j=a_{-j-1}\), \(a_0=1\), and \(a_1=13\). The determinant without the cohomology norm also has zero-mode contributions; an arbitrary bare determinant is not asserted to obey only the displayed local formula.
reconstruction: The precise object is the determinant-line metric developed explicitly in record 655. An area counterterm belongs to the regularization prescription; it is not part of a universal numerical coefficient.
fate: The \(j=0,1\) string calculation is already in \citet[eqs.~(15)--(25)]{polyakov1981quantum}. The full polynomial, in the cotangent-power convention, is read in \citet[(2.21),(3.22) and \S5]{belavinknizhnik1986complex}; that article cites a 1985 preprint without a verified month. E identifies the expository local-anomaly mechanism, not a claim that this later publication proves its precise public-circulation date.
present_status: As of November 2026: The polynomial is standard; it supplies no new unsolved question. The claim is separated from the incorrect operator convention in item 1985-650.3.

title: Integrating the anomaly into a Liouville action
notes: The page identifies curvature with \(\partial\bar\partial\log\theta\) for \(ds^2=\theta|dz|^2\), and integrates to an action with a gradient term and \(\kappa e^\varphi\).
statement: With \(ds^2=\theta|dz|^2\), Gaussian curvature is \(K_G=-2\theta^{-1}\partial_z\partial_{\bar z}\log\theta\). If \(g=e^\varphi g_0\) on a closed surface, a global Liouville functional has a kinetic term, a background-curvature term proportional to \(\int R_{g_0}\varphi\,dA_0\), and possibly a cosmological term \(\mu\int e^\varphi dA_0\). Spectral-determinant identities additionally account for zero modes and normalization constants.
reconstruction: The background metric is needed for a globally meaningful statement; a flat coordinate expression cannot be integrated unchanged over an arbitrary compact surface. The curvature formula in the notes omits both the factor of \(\theta^{-1}\) and the convention-dependent sign/factor.
fate: Polyakov's 1981 action is the immediate source \citep[eqs.~(16),(24)--(25)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: An established anomaly-to-action construction; the bare global equality recorded here is incomplete and its curvature formula is false.

title: Classical Liouville solutions versus the quantum Liouville integral
notes: Evaluating \(\int e^{\mathcal L(\varphi)}\mathcal D\varphi\) is identified with solving the Liouville equation; the needed integral is left to be computed.
statement: The Euler--Lagrange equation specifies stationary configurations of a Liouville action. It does not determine its full quantum functional integral. One rigorous later setting is the sphere with \(0<\gamma<2\), \(\mu>0\), \(Q=2/\gamma+\gamma/2\), distinct insertion points, and charges \(\alpha_i<Q\), \(\sum_i\alpha_i>2Q\). Gaussian multiplicative chaos then defines nonzero finite renormalized Liouville correlations. These are additional hypotheses, not a reading of the notebook's unspecified integral.
reconstruction: The notebook supplies neither insertion data nor coupling regime, contour, or measure. Consequently no single all-genus or all-central-charge quantum problem can be identified with its final sentence.
fate: For the stated sphere setting, \citet[Thm.~3.2 and Def.~3.6]{davidkupiainenrhodesvargas2016liouville} give a rigorous construction (preprint October 2014; journal 2016). This is a precisely limited later realization, not proof of the asserted equivalence.
present_status: As of November 2026: The classical/quantum equivalence is false. A major later construction exists in a specified regime; the original unrestricted request remains unformulated and receives F, rather than an invented C or D problem.

title: Critical dimension and mixed determinant powers
notes: The displayed factor is \([\operatorname{Det}\Delta_1/(\operatorname{Det}\Delta_0)^{d/2}]^{1/2}\), while the following anomaly is proportional to \(13-d/2\), vanishing at \(d=26\).
statement: For \(d\) real scalar matter fields in bosonic string gauge fixing, the nonzero-mode factor is \((\det'_{\mathbb R}P^*P)^{1/2}(\det'\Delta_0)^{-d/2}\), where \(P\) is the trace-free infinitesimal diffeomorphism operator. The ghost contribution has central charge \(-26\), so the total Weyl anomaly is proportional to \(d-26\). Passing to a complex Dolbeault determinant changes the ghost power accordingly.
reconstruction: The outer square root and the scalar exponent in the notebook mix two conventions: without additional definitions the displayed expression does not entail its next coefficient. The conclusion \(d=26\) is correct independently of this shorthand. Vanishing anomaly is not a proof of convergence of the moduli integral.
fate: This critical-dimension cancellation was published in \citet[eqs.~(20)--(25)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Known before the seminar. The number 26 is secure, whereas the exact displayed determinant formula needs repair.

title: Zero modes turn determinants into cohomology lines
notes: The last remark invokes exterior powers of \(H^1(T)\) and \(H^1(\mathcal O)\) when zero modes are restored.
statement: For a closed curve define \(\lambda(E)=\det H^0(E)\otimes(\det H^1(E))^{-1}\). The anomaly-free tangent/scalar combination in this convention is \(\lambda(T)\otimes\lambda(\mathcal O)^{-13}\), or its dual if determinant conventions are reversed. At genus \(g\ge2\), \(H^0(T)=0\), but \(H^0(\mathcal O)\) remains one-dimensional; its norm still matters.
reconstruction: The power 13 and the omitted degree-zero factors are restored. The notebook's informal ratio of two exterior powers is not an exact specification of the string measure.
fate: This is the cohomological determinant framework of \citet[\S\S1--3]{quillen1985determinants}; record 655 supplies the seminar's explicit definition.
present_status: As of November 2026: An established construction with zero-mode factors essential. The later recurrence should be linked at item level.

title: The Polyakov action on a closed surface
notes: The domain is a smooth closed oriented surface, and \(X\) denotes pairs \((x,g)\), with \(x:\Sigma\to\mathbb R^d\) and \(g\) a Riemannian metric. The quadratic action is repeated.
statement: For a closed oriented smooth surface \(\Sigma\), \(g\in\operatorname{Met}(\Sigma)\), and \(x\in C^\infty(\Sigma,\mathbb R^d)\), define \(S(x,g)=\frac12\int_\Sigma|dx|_g^2dA_g\). It is invariant under simultaneous pullback by diffeomorphisms and under \(g\mapsto e^\varphi g\). The notebook omits the inessential factor \(1/2\).
reconstruction: This is the action on parametrized maps with an independent metric. It is not already a measure on embedded or unparametrized surfaces.
fate: A repetition of the construction in \citet[eq.~(6)]{polyakov1981quantum}; earlier seminar occurrences include 1982-569.4.
present_status: As of November 2026: Classical expository setup, with its functional integral still requiring interpretation.

title: Gelfand on a second string scale
notes: Gelfand says strings introduce two constants, not only \(\hbar\), and interprets the second as the thickness of a tube swept in place of a particle path.
statement: A string action has a tension \(T\), conventionally expressed through a length-squared parameter \(\alpha'\) after units and \(\hbar\) are chosen. This parameter is independent of the quantum expansion scale. A literal transverse tube radius is not defined by the zero-thickness world-sheet action written on this page.
reconstruction: Tension is a precise modern interpretation of the extra scale; it is not a claim that the notebook defines a thick-string model or proves an equality between thickness and \(\sqrt{\alpha'}\).
fate: The area coefficient is already present in \citet[eq.~(2)]{polyakov1981quantum}; the tube description is Gelfand's recorded physical analogy.
present_status: As of November 2026: The dimensional interpretation is identifiable; no independent geometric theorem or parameter determination is stated.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Gaussian integration over the embedding coordinates
notes: Integrating \(e^{-\mathcal L(x,g)}\) over one scalar gives \((\operatorname{Det}\Delta_g)^{-1/2}\), and over \(d\) components gives power \(-d/2\).
statement: For a positive definite real \(N\times N\) matrix \(A\), \(\int_{\mathbb R^N}e^{-x^TAx/2}dx=(2\pi)^{N/2}(\det A)^{-1/2}\). For the scalar Laplacian on a closed connected surface, constants form its kernel. After fixing the mean, the spectral analogue uses \(\det'\Delta_g\); integrating unrestricted target translations contributes an infinite volume. The associated normalized Gaussian field has covariance \(\Delta_g^{-1}\) on mean-zero test functions and is distribution valued in dimension two.
reconstruction: The finite-dimensional identity does not construct an infinite-dimensional flat measure \(\mathcal Dx\). The choice to remove the constant mode and the zeta normalization are additions.
fate: Polyakov uses this determinant reduction in 1981 \citep[eq.~(14)]{polyakov1981quantum}. A rigorous fixed-background field is described in \citet[\S2]{davidkupiainenrhodesvargas2016liouville}.
present_status: As of November 2026: The determinant factor is standard once zero modes and normalization are fixed; smooth random embeddings are not obtained from this Gaussian field.

title: A surface analogue of Wiener measure
notes: A bracketed question asks whether there is an analogue of Wiener measure for surfaces.
statement: No single probability problem is determined: the notes do not fix parametrized maps versus images, area versus Dirichlet weight, target dimension, topology, embeddedness, or a discretization. On a fixed closed background surface, a mean-zero Gaussian free field is a well-defined probability measure on distributions; it is not supported on smooth immersed surfaces and is not itself the desired reparametrization quotient.
reconstruction: The fixed-background Gaussian field is a comparison, not an identification of the question. Different surface ensembles cannot be treated as interchangeable versions of one conjecture.
fate: The precise field construction in \citet[\S2]{davidkupiainenrhodesvargas2016liouville} and its interacting sphere construction illustrate two distinct choices.
present_status: As of November 2026: F: the unspecified ensemble prevents a determinate solved/open assessment. The question is retained as a historical occurrence without a manufactured problem ID.

title: A conformal slice must include Teichmüller parameters
notes: For genus at least two, \(M_c\) is described using metrics conformal to a standard curvature \(-1\) metric, and \(M_c\times\operatorname{Diff}(\Sigma)\to M\) is said to cover all metrics.
statement: Each conformal class on a closed oriented surface of genus \(g\ge2\) has a unique curvature \(-1\) metric. Locally in Teichmüller space one may choose a family \(\widehat g(t)\), \(t\in\mathcal T_g\), and express a metric as \(f^*(e^\varphi\widehat g(t))\). A single fixed hyperbolic metric and its conformal multiples, even after diffeomorphisms, do not cover inequivalent conformal structures.
reconstruction: The Teichmüller parameter is the omitted variable. The finite mapping-class quotient and finite automorphism stabilizers also prevent a global Cartesian-product identification.
fate: The explicit moduli-space formulation is checked in \citet[\S2]{belavinknizhnik1986complex}; the classical slice is not a discovery of that 1986 paper.
present_status: As of November 2026: The literal surjectivity statement is false if ``standard'' denotes one metric. Record 652 partially repairs it by fixing a moduli point explicitly.

title: Formal division by the volume of the diffeomorphism group
notes: The metric integral is divided by \(\operatorname{Vol}\operatorname{Diff}(\Sigma)\), and the remaining expression is to be computed on a slice.
statement: In a finite-dimensional free isometric group action, the coarea formula relates orbit integration to a slice Jacobian. In the string calculation the analogous Faddeev--Popov expression is formal: both the metric-space volume and group volume require regularization, and residual stabilizers and moduli must be included.
reconstruction: There is no countably additive infinite-dimensional Haar/Lebesgue volume supplied by the written \(L^2\) metrics. The argument is retained as a computational prescription, not as a measure identity.
fate: The gauge-fixing source is \citet[eqs.~(17)--(23)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: An established formal reduction; its validity does not follow from cancellation of two infinite constants.

title: The assertion that the integral collapses to a small set
notes: The main contribution is said to come from a small set, with everything collapsing to a point.
statement: A localization or saddle-point claim requires a specified family of measures, an asymptotic parameter, an observable, and a topology of convergence. None is given here.
reconstruction: This sentence could refer to a Gaussian saddle, conformal collapse, or a heuristic concentration of random surfaces. The surrounding formulas do not select one.
fate: No exact theorem has been identified. Polyakov's symbolic integral does not supply a proof of the literal concentration statement.
present_status: As of November 2026: Unidentifiable claim (F), not evidence that a precise localization problem remained open.

title: L2 metrics and the infinitesimal diffeomorphism action
notes: The page gives \(L^2\) norms on metric variations and vector fields, and defines \(D\varepsilon\) by differentiating the change of metric under a diffeomorphism.
statement: For a fixed closed surface \((\Sigma,g)\), use \(\langle h,k\rangle=\int\operatorname{tr}(g^{-1}hg^{-1}k)dA\) on symmetric covariant 2-tensors and \(\langle v,w\rangle=\int g(v,w)dA\). Then \((Dv)_{ab}=(\mathcal L_vg)_{ab}=\nabla_av_b+\nabla_bv_a\). Formal adjoints are defined with these pairings. The trace-free gauge operator is \((Pv)_{ab}=Dv_{ab}-(\operatorname{div}v)g_{ab}\).
reconstruction: Covariant indices and the distinction between \(D\) and its trace-free projection \(P\) are made explicit. Both are needed before interpreting the determinant.
fate: These are the geometric operators behind \citet[eqs.~(17)--(21)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Correct geometric constructions, with the projection indispensable for conformal gauge.

title: The square-root Jacobian and the missing finite-dimensional directions
notes: The orbit Jacobian is \((\det D^*D)^{1/2}\), and symmetric 2-tensors are split into conformal and diffeomorphism parts.
statement: For a closed genus-\(g\ge2\) surface, the elliptic decomposition is \(\Gamma(S^2T^*\Sigma)=\{fg\}\oplus\operatorname{im}P\oplus\ker P^*\) after the appropriate Sobolev completion. The last summand is the real space of holomorphic quadratic differentials, dimension \(6g-6\). The nonzero-mode orbit Jacobian is formally \((\det'P^*P)^{1/2}\); Gram determinants for moduli directions must also be retained.
reconstruction: The notebook's two-summand decomposition omits \(\ker P^*\). At genus at least two there are no nonzero conformal Killing vector fields, but the moduli cokernel is still present.
fate: The complete moduli factors are displayed in \citet[\S2]{belavinknizhnik1986complex}.
present_status: As of November 2026: The finite-dimensional missing summand is known and explicit. This is a faithful mathematical error, not an unresolved gauge-fixing question.

title: Trace-free tensors as Beltrami differentials
notes: The symmetric-square representation of rotations is decomposed into a scalar line and a two-dimensional summand; the latter is identified with \(T\otimes\Omega^{0,1}\), and \(D\) is identified with \(\bar\partial\).
statement: On an oriented Riemannian surface the real bundle \(S^2T^*\) splits into its trace and trace-free parts. Raising one index identifies a real trace-free variation with a Beltrami differential in \(T^{1,0}\otimes\Omega^{0,1}\), together with its complex conjugate. In complex coordinates the trace-free infinitesimal action \(P\), rather than the full Lie derivative \(D\), is \(\bar\partial\) on \(T^{1,0}\) up to a fixed real/complex normalization.
reconstruction: The metric identification and conjugate component account for the real ranks. The trace projection is essential; the full Lie derivative includes a scalar divergence term.
fate: This is the Dolbeault description underlying \citet[\S2]{belavinknizhnik1986complex}.
present_status: As of November 2026: The representation-theoretic splitting is correct; the operator equality holds only after the stated projection and normalization.

title: The ghost operator is not the Hodge Laplacian on one-forms
notes: The final page concludes that \(D^*D\) is the ordinary Laplacian on one-forms, on the ground that exterior differentiation and the Lie derivative are dual.
statement: For the full symmetric gradient \((Dv)_{ab}=\partial_av_b+\partial_bv_a\) in a flat coordinate patch, its positive principal symbol is \(2(|\xi|^2I+\xi\otimes\xi)\). The Hodge Laplacian on one-forms has symbol \(|\xi|^2I\). These cannot agree even after one scalar normalization. For the trace-free operator \(P\), the principal symbols are proportional, but curvature terms still distinguish its Laplacian from the Hodge operator.
reconstruction: The principal-symbol calculation is an editorial countercheck: substituting longitudinal and transverse vectors gives different eigenvalue ratios. It avoids relying on an undeclared sign convention for the curvature term. Editorial flat-symbol computation \oursComputed.
fate: \citet[after eq.~(21)]{polyakov1981quantum} explicitly distinguishes the ghost operator from the ordinary vector Laplacian.
present_status: As of November 2026: The literal equality is false and materially affects the anomaly. It is not an unsolved spectral identity.

title: The subspace lattice and the modular identity
notes: Addition and multiplication mean sum and intersection of subspaces. The modular identity is written \(a(ab+c)=ab+ac\), or \(a(b+c)=ab+ac\) when \(b\le a\).
statement: For a vector space \(V\) over a field \(F\), let \(L(V)\) be its lattice of linear subspaces, with \(U\vee W=U+W\), \(U\wedge W=U\cap W\). If \(B\subseteq A\), then \(A\cap(B+C)=B+(A\cap C)\). Substituting \(B=A\cap B'\) gives the first notebook identity.
reconstruction: The operations and order are fixed explicitly. Modularity is weaker than distributivity and does not imply that every modular lattice is a subspace lattice.
fate: Classical background repeated from the seminar's 1973-319.1--2; see \citet[\S1.1]{gelfandponomarev1974modular}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Correct expository identity. The separate representability problem GP-1973-30 is not re-posed here.

title: A computable dimension bound for a failed lattice identity
notes: For terms \(p,q\), the proposed test dimension is \(N=1+\min\{\max(d(p),d(q)),\max(k(p),k(q))\}\), with \(d\) counting sums and \(k\) intersections.
statement: Fix a field \(F\). For finite lattice terms \(p,q\) in finitely many variables, using binary sum and intersection, let \(d(p)\) and \(k(p)\) count occurrences of the two operations in the written term. The identity \(p=q\) holds in all finite-dimensional \(F\)-subspace lattices if and only if it holds in \(L(F^N)\), with the stated \(N\). A failure in larger dimension has a witness in dimension at most \(N\), which embeds in dimension \(N\).
reconstruction: The published Lemma 1 gives the join-count bound. Its proof follows a vector witnessing a failed inclusion and retains only the finitely many vectors needed at joins; duality of finite-dimensional subspace lattices gives the meet-count bound. Taking the smaller bound recovers the notebook's symmetric formula. This last combination is explicitly a reconstruction from the lemma, not a verbatim theorem number. Editorial deduction of the meet bound by duality and of the minimum of the two bounds \ours; the join-bound proof is due to Ryzhikova.
fate: \citet[Lemma~1, pp.~1058--1059]{ryzhikova1987decidability} is the exact later paper. It was received 16 May 1986 and published in 1987; no earlier public preprint was verified.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established by the speaker soon after the talk (A). This is a genuine quantitative bridge from an unbounded-dimensional question to a finite test.

title: Decidability of identities in linear-subspace lattices
notes: Ryzhikova announces an algorithm deciding identities for all finite-dimensional vector spaces. After the dimension reduction, the note invokes Tarski for subspaces of a fixed real \(n\)-space.
statement: For each fixed field \(F\), there is an algorithm that, given two finite sum/intersection terms, decides whether their equality holds for every tuple of subspaces of every finite-dimensional \(F\)-vector space. The identity theory depends only on \(\operatorname{char}F\). In characteristic zero one reduces to a fixed-dimensional real subspace lattice, encodes its incidence relations by polynomial conditions, and applies real-closed-field quantifier elimination. In characteristic \(p>0\), reduction to \(\mathbb F_p\) makes the bounded-dimensional test finite.
reconstruction: The notebook's real-case explanation is expanded using the published field-independence lemmas. The theorem concerns identities, not the full first-order theory of arbitrary-dimensional lattices, word problems for all modular lattices, or efficient complexity bounds.
fate: \citet[main theorem and Lemmas~2--3, pp.~1058--1061]{ryzhikova1987decidability} proves precisely this result; the English translation appeared in 1988.
present_status: As of November 2026: Solved (A), with the exact quantifiers recovered. No unresolved decision problem is inferred from the absence of a complexity estimate.

title: Fuchs repeats the determinant integral on a metric slice
notes: Fuchs starts with \(\int_{M_c}(\operatorname{Det}\Delta)^{-d/2}\nu\), continuing the previous Gaussian reduction.
statement: For a fixed closed oriented surface of genus \(g\ge2\), the formal matter factor is \((\det'\Delta_0)^{-d/2}\). A conformal-gauge slice also carries a ghost Jacobian, Gram factors for moduli, and zero-mode factors. The symbol \(\nu\) alone does not define the resulting measure.
reconstruction: The prime and the distinction between matter and the full measure are supplied. This sentence is Fuchs's recap; the next paragraph is separately attributed to Feigin in the manuscript.
fate: A recurrence of \citet[eqs.~(14),(17)--(23)]{polyakov1981quantum} and of record 651.
present_status: As of November 2026: Identifiable expository formula, conditional on a consistent gauge and regularization.

title: Fixing a conformal structure before integrating the Weyl factor
notes: Feigin fixes a moduli parameter \(t\), writes \(g=e^\varphi g_0\) with \(K(g_0)=-1\), and notes that the moduli space has complex dimension \(3g-3\).
statement: For a closed curve of genus \(g\ge2\), choose a marked complex structure \(t\) and its hyperbolic metric \(g_0(t)\). Metrics in that conformal class are precisely \(e^\varphi g_0(t)\), \(\varphi\in C^\infty(\Sigma,\mathbb R)\). The tangent space to Teichmüller space is \(H^1(\Sigma,T)\), of complex dimension \(3g-3\). The unmarked moduli space is an orbifold/stack quotient, not globally a smooth manifold with one coordinate chart.
reconstruction: The genus restriction and the marked/unmarked distinction make the dimension claim precise. Keeping \(t\) fixed repairs the single-conformal-class ambiguity of record 651, but leaves a later integration over \(t\).
fate: The resulting separation is described explicitly in \citet[\S2]{belavinknizhnik1986complex}; the underlying uniformization and deformation theory are classical.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established geometry. The moduli directions cannot be discarded by calling the Weyl anomaly zero.
speaker: B. L. Feigin

title: The determinant anomaly with spin j
notes: The conformal derivative is written as an area term \((Aj+B)\int\rho\) plus a curvature term \(C(6j^2+6j+1)\int\rho K\); here \(K\) is explicitly Gaussian curvature.
statement: For the determinant of the Dolbeault complex on \(T^j\), completed by its cohomology metrics, the local Weyl anomaly coefficient is \(6j^2+6j+1\). In particular the tangent and scalar coefficients are 13 and 1. Primed determinants and cohomology norms must be treated together; finite area counterterms depend on a common renormalization prescription.
reconstruction: This occurrence corrects the earlier scalar-curvature label but does not specify enough normalization to certify the constants \(A,B,C\). The numerical spin polynomial is distinguished from those unspecified constants.
fate: The earlier Polyakov calculation \citep[eqs.~(15)--(25)]{polyakov1981quantum} is recast in determinant-line language; compare record 655.
present_status: As of November 2026: Known anomaly calculation. The general-spin and zero-mode qualifications are needed before using it as an exact metric identity.
speaker: B. L. Feigin

title: What becomes constant at dimension 26
notes: At \(d=26\) the anomaly cancels, and the notes say that one now integrates a constant.
statement: After consistent matter/ghost normalization and cancellation of any chosen local counterterm, the critical bosonic measure is independent of the Weyl factor at a fixed complex structure. This does not imply constancy as a function on moduli space, finite Weyl-group volume, or convergence at degenerating curves.
reconstruction: ``Constant'' can only mean independent of the conformal representative in the calculation at hand. Degeneration behavior remains a different question.
fate: The cancellation is already in \citet[eq.~(23)]{polyakov1981quantum}. \citet[\S\S3--4]{belavinknizhnik1986complex} subsequently analyze nontrivial moduli dependence and boundary singularities.
present_status: As of November 2026: The restricted constancy statement is correct; an unrestricted constant integrand is false. No solved anomaly calculation is relabeled as an open string-measure problem.
speaker: B. L. Feigin

title: The remaining integral over moduli
notes: The remaining integral over the \((3g-3)\)-dimensional complex moduli space is said still to require computation.
statement: A definite integral requires a specified genus, inserted states or vacuum normalization, determinant-line trivialization, integration cycle, and a prescription near the Deligne--Mumford boundary. The notebook does not choose these. For the bosonic vacuum measure at genus at least two, a later precise result identifies its holomorphic factor, up to normalization, and its double-pole behavior at degenerations; this does not make the unregularized vacuum integral finite.
reconstruction: The later theorem is a constrained comparison to the stated task of computing moduli dependence. It is not an exact solution of an unspecified numerical integral.
fate: \citet[\S\S3--5]{belavinknizhnik1986complex} provides that geometric analysis. Its bibliography cites a Landau Institute preprint from 1985; no month was verified. The full paper was submitted February 1986 and published August 1986.
present_status: As of November 2026: F for the unspecific integral request, with a strong thematic later development. No separate open-problem ID is assigned.
speaker: B. L. Feigin

title: The background-curvature term in the Liouville action
notes: The integrated determinant contains \(\int\varphi\partial\bar\partial\varphi\), \(\int e^\varphi\operatorname{Vol}\), and \(\int\varphi\operatorname{Vol}\), with unspecified constants.
statement: With a fixed hyperbolic background \(g_0\), a global Liouville action has the form \(S_L(\varphi)=a\int|\nabla\varphi|_{g_0}^2dA_0+b\int R_{g_0}\varphi\,dA_0+\mu\int e^\varphi dA_0\), up to a constant and zero-mode conventions. Since \(R_{g_0}\) is constant, the background-curvature term is proportional to the notebook's linear integral.
reconstruction: The sign relating \(\varphi\partial\bar\partial\varphi\) to the positive energy depends on integration conventions; the notes do not fix \(a,b,\mu\). This occurrence restores a term absent from the earlier local formula.
fate: The framework is Polyakov's \citep[eqs.~(16),(24)--(25)]{polyakov1981quantum}. A precise modern action with curvature normalization appears in \citet[eq.~(1.1)]{davidkupiainenrhodesvargas2016liouville}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established action, with its coefficients and zero modes to be fixed before any exact equality is asserted.
speaker: B. L. Feigin

title: Repeating the classical/quantum Liouville equivalence
notes: Solving the Liouville equation is again called equivalent to computing \(\int e^{\mathcal L_j(\varphi)}\mathcal D\varphi\), and the total action is \(\mathcal L_1-\frac d2\mathcal L_0\).
statement: The combined determinant can formally be written as the exponential of the difference of logarithmic determinants, once conventions are consistent. Its stationary equation does not evaluate the full functional integral. A quantum definition additionally needs the integration law, insertions, zero-mode treatment, and a coupling regime.
reconstruction: The exponential rewriting is an algebraic step, whereas the asserted equivalence with a nonlinear PDE is a separate false implication. Item 1985-650.9 gives a precise later sphere construction and its bounds.
fate: The modern construction in \citet[Thm.~3.2, Def.~3.6]{davidkupiainenrhodesvargas2016liouville} makes the distinction explicit; it is not a universal evaluation by classical solutions.
present_status: As of November 2026: The literal equivalence is false. This underdetermined quantum request remains F, without being declared an open problem.
speaker: B. L. Feigin

title: Gauss--Bonnet for tame complete finite-volume manifolds
notes: Under the heading Cheeger/Gromov, \(X\) is complete, \(\operatorname{vol}X<\infty\), \(|K|<1\), and diffeomorphic to the interior of a compact manifold with boundary. The conclusion is \(\int_Xp(\Omega)=\chi(X)\).
statement: Let \(X^{2m}\) be an oriented complete Riemannian manifold of finite volume and uniformly bounded sectional curvature, diffeomorphic to the interior of a compact smooth manifold with boundary. Then its Euler form \(e(TX,\nabla)\), normalized as the Pfaffian in the Chern--Gauss--Bonnet theorem, is integrable and \(\int_Xe(TX,\nabla)=\chi(X)\).
reconstruction: The symbol \(p\) must mean the Euler polynomial here, not an arbitrary characteristic polynomial or a Pontryagin class. The compact-core assumption is retained; finite volume and bounded curvature alone do not justify this Euler-characteristic equality.
fate: \citet[Introduction, pp.~116--117]{cheegergromov1985characteristic} gives the stated tame case and contrasts nontame counterexamples. The paper is dated 1985; no exact circulation day was established.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established result explicitly attributed to others in the talk. E denotes reported existing work; within-year publication ordering is not independently known.

title: Homotopy invariance of the integrated L-form
notes: The second assertion is that \(\int_XL_k(p_1,\ldots,p_k)\) is a homotopy invariant.
statement: For an oriented complete finite-volume \(4k\)-manifold with uniformly bounded sectional curvature, diffeomorphic to the interior of a compact manifold with boundary, its integrated Hirzebruch \(L\)-form depends only on the oriented homotopy type within this class. The differential-form integral converges because the curvature is bounded and volume finite.
reconstruction: The dimension, orientation convention, and all geometric hypotheses carry over from the preceding item. This is not a claim of homotopy invariance for every Pontryagin number on every noncompact manifold.
fate: Exact match to \citet[Thm.~0.6]{cheegergromov1985characteristic}; its accompanying signature/eta relation is eq.~(0.7).
present_status: As of November 2026: A known theorem in the stated class, with topology at infinity essential to its formulation.

title: Cone geometry and the radial regular singular operator
notes: The notes write \(C(Y)=(0,1]\times Y\), \(ds^2=du^2+u^{-2}g_Y\), and a radial Laplacian \(-\partial_u^2+u^{-2}A(u)\). The same \(A(u)\) is also declared an \(L^2\) section.
statement: For a closed Riemannian link \((Y,g_Y)\), the exact metric cone has metric \(du^2+u^2g_Y\). After a degree-dependent unitary transformation of differential forms to a fixed \(L^2(du)\) space, its Hodge Laplacian is a matrix regular singular operator with radial part \(-\partial_u^2\) and an angular operator multiplied by \(u^{-2}\). For an exact cone the angular coefficient is independent of \(u\); more general conic metrics allow variable coefficients and lower-order terms.
reconstruction: The scan confirms the minus sign in the metric exponent: it is a faithful mathematical error, not an OCR error. The angular operator and the section on which it acts are different objects. The unitary density and degree shifts are missing from the notebook.
fate: The exact cone metric and form decomposition are in \citet[Introduction and \S1]{cheeger1983spectral}, received August 1982, published 1983.
present_status: As of November 2026: The cone model is established. The written \(u^{-2}g_Y\) does not describe a cone tip and cannot support the following cone calculation literally.

title: Logarithmic heat asymptotics and link spectral data
notes: The heat trace has powers of \(t^{1/2}\), a \(c\log t\) term, and a constant \(b\), expressed through \(\zeta_Y(-1)\) and residues at odd integers.
statement: For a compact space with isolated exact conic singularities and a fixed admissible self-adjoint Hodge-Laplacian realization, Cheeger's heat expansion includes ordinary local powers and additional constant and logarithmic contributions. The singular terms are determined by the spectrum of shifted angular operators on the link. In middle degrees, ideal boundary conditions must be specified when uniqueness fails; regular values of a zeta function may need replacement by finite parts at poles.
reconstruction: The notebook does not define whether \(\lambda_j\) are eigenvalues of the link Laplacian, its shifted square root, or the angular matrix operator. Therefore its numerical coefficients \(b_j\), evaluation at \(-1\), and residue arguments are not certified as an exact formula for an unshifted link zeta function. The regular \(t^0\) term must not be counted twice.
fate: \citet[Thms.~4.1 and 4.4, especially eq.~(4.38)]{cheeger1983spectral} supplies the precise expansion and spectral correction.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established spectral geometry. The structural statement matches, while the compressed coefficient formula needs the omitted angular and domain conventions.

title: The signature operator and its eta correction
notes: For \(\dim X=4k\), the signature operator is \(d+\delta:\Lambda_+^*\to\Lambda_-^*\), with index \(\int_XL+\eta_Y(B)\); on the cone it is written \(-\partial_u+u^{-1}B\). The \(L\)-form is said to vanish on the cone.
statement: Let a compact oriented \(4k\)-manifold with boundary be completed by exact cone tips over its closed links. The natural \(L^2\) signature equals the signature of the image of relative middle cohomology in absolute middle cohomology. It is given by the interior \(L\)-integral plus a spectral boundary correction. With the usual outward-boundary odd-signature convention this is written \(\operatorname{sign}M=\int_ML-\eta_{\mathrm{sign}}(\partial M)\). On an exact cone the \(L\)-density vanishes; the remaining tip contribution is spectral.
reconstruction: Changing link orientation or the sign of \(B\) changes the displayed eta sign. For a general Dirac APS index one instead encounters the reduced expression \((\eta+h)/2\). Clifford multiplication, unitary radial rescaling, and degree shifts are needed to interpret the radial formula; the shorthand is not a universal scalar equality.
fate: \citet[\S6, eqs.~(6.1),(6.4),(6.14)--(6.15)]{cheeger1983spectral} gives the exact signature interpretation.
present_status: As of November 2026: Known before the talk. Its eta term is meaningful only with the boundary operator, orientation, and realization fixed.

title: An index formula for general Fuchs-type operators
notes: For \(D=\partial_u^n+\sum u^{i-n}\partial_u^iA_j\), with differential operators on \(Y\), the notebook asks \ru{индекс --- ?}. It points to the eta term in Cheeger's example.
statement: A well-posed version fixes a compact manifold with isolated conic ends, Hermitian bundles, and an elliptic Fuchs-type operator \(D=u^{-\nu}\sum_{k=0}^\mu A_k(u)(-u\partial_u)^k\), \(\nu>0\), in the cone-elliptic calculus. Its ordinary and rescaled principal symbols must be invertible away from zero. One also specifies a closed domain between the minimal and maximal \(L^2\) domains. These extensions are Fredholm; when the \(A_k\) are constant near each tip, the minimal-domain index is the interior local index contribution plus a generalized eta invariant of the Mellin symbol. Enlarging the domain adds its finite dimension relative to the minimal domain.
reconstruction: Ellipticity, compactness, bundles, density, and domain are supplied requirements. The mixed indices \(i,j\) and missing summation limits in the notebook do not specify a single operator. The reconstructed problem asks for the general index mechanism, rather than a numerical index without data.
fate: A precise later solution is \citet[Prop.~1.3.16, Cor.~2.4.7 and Thm.~2.4.8]{lesch1997fuchs}. The text derives from a June 1993 habilitation, appeared as a July 1996 preprint, and was published in 1997.
present_status: As of November 2026: B: the identifiable regular singular index program has an established realization under explicit hypotheses. No exact unproved remainder is asserted for the notebook's underspecified formula.

title: The endpoint condition does not specify a general cone domain
notes: The index is taken on functions satisfying \(\lim_{u\to0}u^{-1/2}\varphi(u)=\lim_{u\to0}u^{1/2}\varphi'(u)\).
statement: An elliptic regular singular operator generally needs conditions on the coefficients of its indicial asymptotics, depending on the angular spectrum. For the scalar repeated-root model, solutions may contain \(a\sqrt u+b\sqrt u\log u\). The two written limits both exist finitely only if \(b=0\), and then are \(a\) and \(a/2\); the stated equality forces \(a=0\). It is therefore not the usual condition merely excluding the logarithmic branch.
reconstruction: This substitution is an editorial check of the formula, not an identification of the intended operator. Since its angular mode and extension are not named, a unique corrected endpoint condition cannot be recovered. Editorial endpoint-asymptotics substitution \oursComputed.
fate: The dependence of domains on indicial data is described in \citet[\S1.3 and Prop.~1.3.16]{lesch1997fuchs}.
present_status: As of November 2026: F for the intended extension; the displayed condition cannot serve as a universal conic boundary condition.

title: Finite L2 kernels for invariant operators require ellipticity
notes: For finite-volume \(X=K\backslash G/\Gamma\), locally defined bundles and a locally invariant operator \(D\), the notes assert finite-dimensional \(\ker\bar D\) and \(\ker\bar D^*\), then define their dimension difference.
statement: For a specified closed densely defined operator \(D:L^2(E)\to L^2(F)\), the \(L^2\) index \(\dim\ker D-\dim\ker D^*\) is defined when both dimensions are finite. Local invariance alone does not imply this: the zero operator on a positive-dimensional finite-volume locally symmetric manifold is invariant and has infinite-dimensional kernel. Relevant theorems concern elliptic homogeneous or generalized Dirac operators with controlled cusp geometry and specified realizations.
reconstruction: The manuscript does not state the needed ellipticity or operator class, and the bundle annotation is uncertain. We do not replace it by an unrestricted theorem about all invariant differential operators. Editorial zero-operator counterexample \ours.
fate: \citet{muller1987cusps} treats rank-one cusp geometry and generalized Dirac operators. Its publisher description and chapter list were checked; the full operator theorem was not read.
present_status: As of November 2026: The broad literal assertion is false. The established analytic program is identifiable, but this specific scope is only indirectly matched.

title: Hilbert modular surfaces and the one-cusp qualification
notes: The example is \((\mathbb H\times\mathbb H)/\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathcal O_F)\), \(F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt D)\), followed by ``only 1 cusp''. The cusp lattice and unit group are \(M=\mathcal O_F\), \(V=\mathcal O_F^{*2}\).
statement: Let \(F\) be a real quadratic field and let its two real embeddings define the action of \(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathcal O_F)\) on \(\mathbb H^2\). This finite-volume quotient has cusp classes indexed by the ideal classes of \(F\); it has one cusp when the ordinary class number is one. The full quotient may have finite isotropy. One must either work with an orbifold index or pass to a torsion-free subgroup, which may introduce more cusps.
reconstruction: The notebook does not impose class number one or remove torsion. The displayed \((M,V)\) describes a chosen standard cusp, not automatically all cusps of every Hilbert modular surface.
fate: The intended application is identifiable with \citet{muller1984signature}, a 1984 paper verified in the author's bibliography. The full paper was inaccessible in this run.
present_status: As of November 2026: The geometry is classical; the one-cusp assertion is false without a field/subgroup qualification. Publication match is partial because the exact setup was not recovered from the full source.

title: The cusp signature defect and the Shimizu L-series
notes: The index is written \(\frac13\int_Xp_1-\frac1{2\pi}L(M,V,1)\operatorname{vol}(\mathbb R^2/M)\). The series is \(\sum\operatorname{sign}N(\mu)/|N(\mu)|^s\), but its summation domain ends with the unexplained \(N_F\).
statement: For a rank-two lattice \(M\) in a real quadratic field and a finite-index group \(V\) of totally positive norm-one units preserving it, define \(L(M,V,s)=\sum_{\mu\in(M\setminus\{0\})/V}\operatorname{sign}N_{F/\mathbb Q}(\mu)|N_{F/\mathbb Q}(\mu)|^{-s}\), initially where it converges absolutely. The orbit quotient is necessary: summing over all nonzero lattice points repeats each norm infinitely often. Relating its continued value at 1 to a cusp signature defect also requires choices of cusp orientation, lattice/covolume normalization, and index realization.
reconstruction: The orbit domain is a mathematical emendation, not a reading of the written \(N_F\). The numerical coefficient \(1/(2\pi)\) in the notebook has not been verified in Müller's original paper, so it is not promoted to a fully checked modern theorem.
fate: The title and scope of \citet{muller1984signature} identify this application; the author's later \citet{muller1987cusps} includes the Hirzebruch conjecture in its final chapter. Only primary metadata was accessible for these exact formulas.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established subject and strong publication identification, but exact handwritten normalization remains unverified. This is not classified as an open number-theoretic problem.

title: The Dolbeault complex of a tangent tensor power
notes: The sequence is \(0\to H^0(T^j)\to\Gamma(T^j)\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\Gamma(T^j\otimes\Omega^{0,1})\to H^1(T)\to0\).
statement: On a closed smooth complex curve and for \(j\in\mathbb Z\), the Dolbeault resolution gives \(0\to H^0(T^j)\to C^\infty(T^j)\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}C^\infty(T^j\otimes\Omega^{0,1})\to H^1(T^j)\to0\). The final arrow is the quotient by the image of \(\bar\partial\).
reconstruction: The final cohomology group must retain the exponent \(j\). The scan confirms that it is absent in the notebook, so this is an emendation of the mathematical record.
fate: The complex is the standard setting of \citet[\S1]{quillen1985determinants}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Known Dolbeault theory; the last-term typo is substantive when \(j\ne1\).

title: Harmonic representatives give cohomology norms
notes: Hermitian metrics on both spaces induce metrics on \(H^0(T^j)\) and \(H^1(T^j)\); \(\ker\bar\partial\bar\partial^*\) is identified with the latter.
statement: For a closed Riemann surface with smooth compatible metrics, \(H^0(T^j)=\ker\bar\partial\), and Hodge theory identifies \(H^1(T^j)\) with \(\ker\bar\partial^*\) on \((0,1)\)-forms, equivalently with \(\ker(\bar\partial\bar\partial^*)\). The \(L^2\) inner products on these finite-dimensional harmonic spaces define Hodge norms on their determinant lines.
reconstruction: The compact boundaryless hypothesis makes the harmonic representative unique; no boundary condition is left implicit.
fate: This construction is described in \citet[\S3]{quillen1985determinants}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established and correct with the closed-surface hypothesis.

title: The determinant of cohomology and its dual convention
notes: The notes define \(\operatorname{Det}T^j=\Lambda^{\max}H^0(T^j)\otimes(\Lambda^{\max}H^1(T^j))^*\), calling this Quillen's terminology.
statement: Set \(\lambda(T^j)=\det H^0(T^j)\otimes\det H^1(T^j)^{-1}\), with \(\det0=\mathbb C\). This is one complex line. Quillen's operator determinant line for \(D=\bar\partial\) is \(\operatorname{DET}D=(\det\ker D)^{-1}\otimes\det\operatorname{coker}D=\lambda(T^j)^{-1}\). Both conventions are legitimate, but their metrics and sections are dual.
reconstruction: The duality is a convention clarification, not an error in the notebook's definition. In an index-zero family the canonical determinant section is holomorphic in Quillen's convention; one must not transfer that assertion unchanged to its reciprocal.
fate: The convention is explicitly checked against \citet[\S\S1--2]{quillen1985determinants}.
present_status: As of November 2026: A standard determinant line; the dual convention is recorded so subsequent signs and powers remain traceable.

title: The zeta correction of the Hodge metric
notes: If \(\varepsilon\) is the Hermitian metric on \(\operatorname{Det}T^j\), the ``Ray--Singer torsion'' metric is \(\varepsilon/\operatorname{Det}\Delta_j\).
statement: On the cohomological convention \(\lambda(T^j)\), the squared Quillen norm is \(\|\cdot\|_Q^2=\|\cdot\|_{L^2}^2/\det'\Delta_j\). Equivalently, on Quillen's dual line it is the Hodge squared norm multiplied by \(\det'\Delta_j\). This definition includes nontrivial kernels through the determinant of cohomology.
reconstruction: ``Metric'' is read as the Hermitian pairing or squared norm, not its square root. The prime and the dual convention explain the notebook's division. This is holomorphic analytic torsion of a Dolbeault complex, not an assertion of metric independence for ordinary de Rham torsion in every dimension.
fate: Exact match after dualization to \citet[\S3, metric formula and Proposition]{quillen1985determinants}, published before the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established construction. The factor is consistent and should not be corrected merely because a different convention multiplies by the determinant.

title: Anomaly-free tensor products of determinant lines
notes: For integers \(j_\alpha,k_\alpha\), the product metric on \(\bigotimes_\alpha(\operatorname{Det}T^{j_\alpha})^{k_\alpha}\) is unchanged under conformal variation if \(\sum_\alpha(6j_\alpha^2+6j_\alpha+1)k_\alpha=0\).
statement: For a fixed closed complex curve, use induced metrics on the integer powers \(T^{j_\alpha}\) and the canonical zeta-corrected determinant-cohomology metrics, with one consistent normalization. Their local conformal variation is a common Liouville variation multiplied by \(a_{j_\alpha}=6j_\alpha^2+6j_\alpha+1\). Consequently the product metric is independent of the conformal representative whenever \(\sum k_\alpha a_{j_\alpha}=0\). Negative powers mean dual lines. Arbitrary independent finite counterterms are excluded.
reconstruction: The common normalization and zero-mode cohomology factors are supplied. This is a sufficient anomaly-cancellation condition, not a claim that the determinant lines are individually metric independent or that all moduli-space functions are constant.
fate: The ingredients are the pre-talk Quillen metric and Polyakov anomaly \citep{quillen1985determinants,polyakov1981quantum}; \citet[\S\S3,5]{belavinknizhnik1986complex} gives the ensuing string determinant-line formulation. General-spin coefficients there use \(K^n\), so \(n=-j\).
present_status: As of November 2026: An established consequence of the local anomaly calculation (E), with the later geometric formulation distinguished from the already known cancellation mechanism.

title: Descent to the moduli stack and the Faltings comparison
notes: The one-dimensional spaces form a line bundle on the moduli space of genus-\(g\) curves. The resulting metric depends only on complex structure. A similar construction is tentatively attributed to Faltings.
statement: For a smooth proper family of complex curves, determinant of cohomology forms a line bundle even when individual cohomology dimensions jump. The anomaly-free tensor product is natural under isomorphisms and therefore defines a Hermitian line on the moduli stack; on a fine level cover it is an ordinary line bundle. Descent to the coarse moduli space additionally requires trivial stabilizer action on the fibers.
reconstruction: The notebook's word ``manifold'' suppresses automorphisms. The uncertain name is retained as a comparison, not identified with a specific Faltings theorem or a proof of the exact metric assertion.
fate: The family construction is in \citet[\S\S2--3]{quillen1985determinants}; the string-moduli line is in \citet[\S5]{belavinknizhnik1986complex}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established determinant geometry. The Faltings attribution is not sufficiently specific for a separate publication match.

title: Perfect elements and compatible direct-sum decompositions
notes: An element \(a\in L\) is perfect if every representation \(\rho:L\to L(V)\) admits a complement \(U\) to \(\rho(a)\) splitting every \(\rho(x)\). Equivalently, in every indecomposable representation \(\rho(a)\) is zero or all of \(V\).
statement: For a modular lattice \(L\), quantify over every field \(F\) and every finite-dimensional representation \(\rho:L\to L(V)\). Perfection means there exists \(V=\rho(a)\oplus U\) with \(\rho(x)=(\rho(x)\cap\rho(a))\oplus(\rho(x)\cap U)\) for every \(x\in L\). This is equivalent to \(\rho(a)\in\{0,V\}\) for every indecomposable such representation, by decomposing a finite-dimensional representation into indecomposables.
reconstruction: Finite dimensionality is essential to the elementary decomposition argument and is explicit in the published definition. It should not be silently replaced by arbitrary infinite-dimensional lattice representations.
fate: Exact definition and equivalence in \citet[\S1.2]{gelfandponomarev1974modular}; earlier occurrence 1973-319.7.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established expository material (E); the present speaker explicitly credits the 1974 work.

title: Modular lattice axioms and free generators
notes: Associativity, commutativity, idempotence, absorption, the induced order, and \(a\le b\Rightarrow b(a+c)=a+bc\) are listed. The free modular lattice \(D^r\) has generators \(e_1,\ldots,e_r\).
statement: A lattice has associative commutative idempotent join and meet satisfying absorption. The additional implication \(a\le b\Rightarrow b\wedge(a\vee c)=a\vee(b\wedge c)\) is modularity. The free modular lattice \(D^r\) has the universal property that any assignment of its \(r\) generators to a modular lattice extends uniquely to a lattice homomorphism.
reconstruction: The notebook's heading ``definition of a lattice'' includes the extra modular axiom. Free modular lattices are not free distributive lattices, and equality in \(D^r\) is stronger than equality in every finite-dimensional linear representation.
fate: \citet[\S\S1.1--1.3]{gelfandponomarev1974modular}; compare occurrences 1973-319.1--4.
present_status: As of November 2026: Standard definitions; no representability or word-problem conjecture is posed on this page.

title: The first upper Boolean cubicle
notes: Put \(h_t(1)=\sum_{j\ne t}e_j\). These generate \(B^+(1)\), a Boolean algebra. The illustrated list starts with \(0\) and then gives products of the \(h_t\).
statement: In the free modular lattice with \(r\ge4\) generators, the sublattice generated by \(h_t(1)=\bigvee_{j\ne t}e_j\) is a Boolean lattice with \(2^r\) elements, and every one of its elements is perfect. Its top is \(\bigvee_je_j\), and its bottom is \(\bigwedge_th_t(1)\). This is a relative Boolean algebra: its bottom need not be the bottom of the ambient free lattice.
reconstruction: The lower bound on \(r\) keeps the statement in the nondegenerate infinite-family setting. In the enumeration the empty meet is the cubicle top, not zero. Under a representation sending every \(e_j\) to the same nonzero space, the cubicle bottom also maps to that space, so identifying it with a universal zero is impossible. Editorial all-generators-equal representation check \ours; the cubicle theorem is due to Gelfand--Ponomarev.
fate: \citet[\S1.3 and \S\S3--4]{gelfandponomarev1974modular}; this repeats 1973-319.9.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established Boolean cubicle construction. The notebook's endpoint notation needs correction, not a new theorem.
